question.problem: Consider the equation $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})+1=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3})+1 & =0 \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3}) & =-1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3}) & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{7\pi }{3}) & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{7\pi }{3} & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x-\frac{7\pi }{3} & =\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{25\pi }{12}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{43\pi }{12}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{25\pi }{24}+n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{43\pi }{24}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{25\pi }{24}+\frac{24n\pi }{24} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{43\pi }{24}+\frac{24n\pi }{24} \\ x & =\frac{\pi (25+24n)}{24} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi (43+24n)}{24}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{25\pi }{24}$ and $x=\frac{43\pi }{24}$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{24}$ and $x=\frac{19\pi }{24}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{24},\frac{19\pi }{24},\frac{25\pi }{24},\frac{43\pi }{24}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{24}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{25\pi }{24},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=\frac{\pi }{24}+\frac{25\pi }{24}=\frac{26\pi }{24}=\frac{13\pi }{12}.
$$
